author: Wapakoneta Daily News
title: Fisher of Men Charters Appoints Captain Ben Biddle as New Leader; Captain Randy Elliott to Head Inshore Division
text:
North Myrtle Beach, SC - April 23, 2025 - Fisher of Men Charters, a locally-operated charter rooted in the fishing traditions of the Grand Strand, is entering a new chapter of its leadership to carry forward a legacy of outstanding service and deep-sea adventure. Captain Ben Biddle has officially stepped into the role of lead captain at Fisher of Men Charters, taking the helm from longtime mentor and founder Captain Randy Elliot, who now leads the inshore division under Fisher of Men Inshore Charters.
This transition reflects not only the strength of the company’s succession planning but also its commitment to providing guests with an authentic and skillfully guided experience on water.
Captain Ben Biddle Leads Fisher of Men Charters
Captain Ben’s promotion follows 15 years of working alongside Captain Randy, where he gained extensive experience supporting offshore trips, managing vessel operations, and interacting with guests from all over the country. He now leads offshore charter trips out of Little River Inlet with the same focus on professionalism that has come to define the brand.
“Ben has earned his stripes through years of dedication, patience, and hands-on experience on the water,” said Captain Randy. “He knows the rhythms of the Atlantic, understands what our clients are looking for, and has what it takes to lead this next chapter of Fisher of Men Charters.”
Fisher of Men Charters offers offshore deep-sea fishing trips tailored to small groups looking to explore the Atlantic. Captain Ben’s calm presence, deep local knowledge, and strong focus on safety and personalization will enable him to deliver a productive and enjoyable charter. With his appointment, Fisher of Men Charters remains deeply connected to its roots, charting a future guided by experience and a shared passion for fishing.
Captain Randy Elliott Shifts Focus to Inshore Charters
While stepping back from full-time offshore operations, Captain Randy will continue to remain involved. He will lead select trips and support the business with the passion and knowledge that has earned Fisher of Men Charters its great reputation.
Captain Randy will focus his attention on Fisher of Men Inshore Charters, which provides private inshore fishing excursions ideal for families and those seeking a laid-back introduction to the thrill of coastal fishing.
He has more than 50 years of experience fishing the local waters – 30 years in charter – and is widely recognized for his deep knowledge of the Little River Inlet ecosystem and surrounding waters.
“Fishing these waters has been my life’s work,” said Captain Randy. “It’s a privilege to continue sharing that with families, children, and first-time anglers who want a safe and fun experience close to shore.”
The Fisher of Men Charters and Fisher of Men Inshore Charters operate out of the Little River waterfront, serving a wide coastal area, including Ocean Isle Beach, Sunset Beach, and Calabash. Both charter operations are fully licensed and equipped to deliver a private fishing experience. They provide all the rods, reels, bait, tackle, and safety gear needed for a complete day on the water.
Both divisions will continue operating under the Fisher of Men umbrella, providing tailored fishing experiences that reflect the needs and preferences of each group.
For more information or to book a charter, please visit https://www.fisherofmencharter.com and https://fisherofmeninshorecharters.com.
About Fisher of Men Charters
Fisher of Men Charters was founded by Captain Randy Elliott, whose lifelong passion for fishing and connection to the sea continue to shape the company’s values today. Based in Little River, South Carolina, the charter service is committed to providing memorable and rewarding fishing experiences for anglers of all ages and skill levels. Fisher of Men Charters offers a professional, personalized approach that highlights both the beauty of the ocean and the thrill of the catch.
